citation: E. Escoto, A.-L. Viotti, S. Alisauskas, H. Tünnermann, I. Hartl and C. M. Heyl, "Temporal quality of post-compressed pulses at large compression factors", J. Opt. Soc. Am. B 39, 1694 (2022)
fullTextRead: arXiv:2201.05836v1 (the journal version was not compared; locations below are sections and equations of the preprint)
topic: post-compression: temporal quality after SPM broadening and linear compression

referenceNumbers.value: error below 5 % for FTL and GDD-only compression up to B = 40 rad
up to 100 rad: below 2 % (FTL), just above 10 % (GDD only)
the GDD that maximises the peak power
secondary pulses appear roughly when C > 2
a chirped Gaussian with gamma / sigma^2 = +-5 is almost 14 times longer
energy and intensity ratios degrade much faster with increasing C for a chirped input
730 fs, 1030 nm, 2 m Ar MPC: energy ratio 92 % (2 mJ) and 83 % (3 mJ); peak power boost ~10 and ~14
referenceNumbers.status: verified in text, not reproduced (cell parameters not given)

referenceNumbers.value: optimal cascading ratio C1 = C2; dual-stage better than single-stage unless the ratio exceeds 10

assumptions: The paper's model (Eq. 1): pure SPM of a Gaussian, no dispersion during broadening, no losses. Here: a 1 mm Kerr plate with a constant index, constant beam area, no Raman, no self-steepening, 1 ps input at 1030 nm (the results are dimensionless in t / FWHM_in).
FWHM means the intensity FWHM of the main peak (half-maximum crossings next to the maximum).
Intensity ratio: the highest local maximum of the power other than the main peak, above 1e-5 of it.
Chirped input: GDD = +-tau^2 (gamma / sigma^2 = +-1); C is taken against the transform-limited input duration, as in the paper.
